chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya al-Azraq narrated from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who is killed while owing a debt and leaving no wealth, and his family takes the blood money from his killer: are they required to settle his debt? He said: "Yes."
I said: "Even though he left nothing behind?" He said: "They only took his blood money, so they must settle his debt."

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood money paid for the killing
key_terms.دِيَتَهُ: his blood money, received on account of his death
key_terms.مَالًا: financial property or wealth left behind
key_terms.يَقْضُوا: to discharge or repay an obligation

ai.seo_question: If a murdered person left debts but no property, must his family pay the debt from the diyyah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a slain person who dies in debt and leaves no property behind. If his family receives the diyyah, they are obligated to use it to repay his debt, since the diyyah stands as wealth taken on account of him.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5532 - Safwan ibn Yahya Al-Azraq narrated from Abu Al-Hasan (as), regarding a man who was killed while owing a debt and left behind no wealth. His family took the blood money (diyyah) from his killer. Should they use it to settle his debt?

I asked: "Even though he left nothing behind?"
Imam (as) replied: "They took his blood money, so they must use it to settle his debt."
